date_note: FinCEN's statement was issued on Tuesday per Türkiye Gazetesi's article of 25 November; resolved to 24 November.
geo_basis: agency headquarters, Washington DC (US Treasury unit)
title: FinCEN says an unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of its systems
summary: CyberScoop reports FinCEN, a US Treasury unit, said an unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of its systems and it took some offline as a precaution. Cyber Security News says a FinCEN official told Reuters no breach of the BSA or beneficial ownership databases has been found so far. Daily Security Review says the relief order cites a service disruption, and FinCEN has not said whether filing failures since November 18 are related.
plain: FinCEN, a US Treasury unit, says an unauthorized party got into a limited subset of its systems and it took some offline. Daily Security Review says FinCEN has not said whether filing failures since November 18 are related.
exec: FinCEN says some services may be temporarily unavailable and it is extending deadlines for affected filers.
action: No action needed; for awareness. FinCEN says it is extending deadlines for filers affected by the disruption.

sources.name: Türkiye Gazetesi: ABD'nin kritik kurumlarına peş peşe siber saldırı!

validation.note: CyberScoop (relaying FinCEN's notice) and Türkiye Gazetesi are independent publishers stating the core fact; AITNews relays The Verge. FinCEN's own notice was not read. DataBreaches.net returned 403 and Punto Informatico reset the connection.

review.note: Checked CyberScoop, Cyber Security News, GovInfoSecurity: limited subset, offline systems, deadlines, Reuters-relayed no BSA/beneficial ownership breach found
